items.title: Piecewise cubic Hermite interpolant

references.title: Carl R. de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines, revised edition, Chapter IV, pp. 39–40

items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ be an integer, let $x_0<\cdots<x_N$ be real nodes, let $y_0,\ldots,y_N\in\mathbb R$ be values, and let $m_0,\ldots,m_N\in\mathbb R$ be prescribed slopes. For $0\le i<N$ put $h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i>0$ and $t=(x-x_i)/h_i$ on $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$. Define
$$H_{00}(t)=2t^3-3t^2+1,\quad H_{01}(t)=-2t^3+3t^2,\quad H_{10}(t)=t^3-2t^2+t,\quad H_{11}(t)=t^3-t^2.$$
The cubic Hermite piece on $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$ is
$$P_i(x)=y_iH_{00}(t)+y_{i+1}H_{01}(t)+h_im_iH_{10}(t)+h_im_{i+1}H_{11}(t).$$
The piecewise cubic Hermite interpolant is the function whose restriction to each such interval is $P_i$; adjacent pieces use their common prescribed value $y_i$ at a shared node. The slopes $m_i$ are input data, not values inferred from neighboring pieces.

items.title: Piecewise Bernstein representation

references.title: Rida T. Farouki, The Bernstein polynomial basis: a centennial retrospective, Computer Aided Geometric Design 29 (2012), pp. 379–419

items.statement:
Let $s\ge1$ be an integer and let $a=x_0<\cdots<x_s=b$ be a finite partition, and on each cell $[x_i,x_{i+1}]$ choose an integer degree $n_i\ge0$ and real controls $c_{i,0},\ldots,c_{i,n_i}$. For $t=(x-x_i)/(x_{i+1}-x_i)\in[0,1]$, define the Bernstein basis polynomial
$$B_{k,n_i}(t)=\iota\binom{n_i}{k}t^k(1-t)^{n_i-k},\qquad 0\le k\le n_i,$$
where $\binom{n_i}{k}$ is the natural binomial coefficient from [[def-binomial-coefficient]], $\iota$ is the canonical embedding of [[def-canonical-natural]] into $\mathbb R$, and finite sums use [[def-finite-sum]]. The cell polynomial is $p_i(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n_i}c_{i,k}B_{k,n_i}(t)$. These cell polynomials form a piecewise Bernstein representation. To require continuity at a shared node, impose the additional endpoint-control condition $c_{i,n_i}=c_{i+1,0}$; continuity is not part of the representation unless that condition is imposed.

For degree two this formula reads $p_i(x)=c_{i,0}(1-t)^2+\iota\binom21\,c_{i,1}t(1-t)+c_{i,2}t^2$.

items.title: Interpolation, C1 matching, and cubic reproduction for Hermite pieces

references.title: Carl R. de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines, revised edition, Chapter IV, pp. 39–40

items.statement: For the data in [[def-piecewise-cubic-hermite-interpolant]], each piece has the prescribed endpoint values and slopes: $P_i(x_i)=y_i$, $P_i(x_{i+1})=y_{i+1}$, $P_i'(x_i)=m_i$, and $P_i'(x_{i+1})=m_{i+1}$. The resulting interpolant is $C^1$ on $[x_0,x_N]$ (with the corresponding one-sided derivatives at the endpoints). On a single interval, if the four prescribed endpoint data are the values and derivatives of a polynomial $q$ of degree at most three, then $P_i=q$ on that interval.

items.title: A sufficient monotonicity square for cubic Hermite interpolation

references.title: F. N. Fritsch and J. Butland, A Method for Constructing Local Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolants, SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 5 (1984), pp. 300–304

items.statement: Let $p$ be the single Hermite piece from [[def-piecewise-cubic-hermite-interpolant]] on $[x_0,x_1]$, with $h=x_1-x_0>0$, endpoint values $y_0,y_1$, slopes $m_0,m_1$, and secant $d=(y_1-y_0)/h$. If $d\ne0$ and $\alpha=m_0/d$, $\beta=m_1/d$ both lie in $[0,3]$, then $p$ is monotone from $y_0$ to $y_1$ and stays between those values. If $d=0$ and $m_0=m_1=0$, then $p$ is constant.

items.title: PCHIP slope selection

references.title: F. N. Fritsch and J. Butland, A Method for Constructing Local Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolants, SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 5 (1984), pp. 300–304

items.statement:
**Inputs:** An integer $n\ge2$, strictly increasing real nodes $x_0<\cdots<x_{n-1}$, and real values $y_0,\ldots,y_{n-1}$. All operations here are over the real numbers.

**Output:** Slopes $m_0,\ldots,m_{n-1}$ and the piecewise cubic Hermite interpolant determined by these nodes, values, and slopes under [[def-piecewise-cubic-hermite-interpolant]].

Put $h_i=x_{i+1}-x_i>0$ and $d_i=(y_{i+1}-y_i)/h_i$ for $0\le i<n-1$. Write $\operatorname{sgn}(r)\in\{-1,0,1\}$ for the sign of a real number.

- If $n=2$, set $m_0=m_1=d_0$.
- If $n\ge3$, for each interior node $1\le k\le n-2$, set $m_k=0$ when $d_{k-1}d_k\le0$. When $d_{k-1}d_k>0$, put $w_1=2h_k+h_{k-1}$, $w_2=h_k+2h_{k-1}$, and
  $$m_k=\frac{w_1+w_2}{w_1/d_{k-1}+w_2/d_k}.$$
- For $n\ge3$, at the left endpoint compute
  $$\widehat m_0=\frac{(2h_0+h_1)d_0-h_0d_1}{h_0+h_1}.$$
  Set $m_0=0$ if $\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat m_0)\ne\operatorname{sgn}(d_0)$. Otherwise set $m_0=3d_0$ if $d_0d_1<0$ and $|\widehat m_0|>3|d_0|$; in all remaining cases set $m_0=\widehat m_0$.
- For $n\ge3$, at the right endpoint compute
  $$\widehat m_{n-1}=\frac{(2h_{n-2}+h_{n-3})d_{n-2}-h_{n-2}d_{n-3}}{h_{n-2}+h_{n-3}}.$$
  Apply the preceding clip and cap rule with $d_0,d_1$ replaced by $d_{n-2},d_{n-3}$ and $m_0,\widehat m_0$ replaced by $m_{n-1},\widehat m_{n-1}$.

For $n\ge3$, the algorithm returns the Hermite pieces from the stated values and selected slopes. The two-node branch is the line through the two input points.

items.title: Bernstein control values bound a piecewise polynomial

references.title: Rida T. Farouki, The Bernstein polynomial basis: a centennial retrospective, Computer Aided Geometric Design 29 (2012), pp. 379–419

items.statement: On each cell of a representation from [[def-piecewise-bernstein-representation]], the polynomial value lies between the minimum and maximum of that cell's controls. In particular, nonnegative controls imply a nonnegative polynomial throughout the cell. If every cell has nonnegative controls and adjacent endpoint controls agree, the piecewise function is continuous and nonnegative on the entire partition. This is a control-value guarantee; positivity at a finite set of sample nodes alone is not among the hypotheses.

items.title: PCHIP slope selection has no zero denominator

references.title: F. N. Fritsch and J. Butland, A Method for Constructing Local Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolants, SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 5 (1984), pp. 300–304

items.statement: For every admissible input to [[alg-pchip-slope-selection]], each branch is defined over $\mathbb R$ and every selected slope is finite; in particular, the algorithm never divides by zero.

items.title: PCHIP endpoint slopes lie in the Hermite monotonicity square

references.title: F. N. Fritsch and J. Butland, A Method for Constructing Local Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolants, SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 5 (1984), pp. 300–304

items.statement: For any input to [[alg-pchip-slope-selection]], consider an interval with secant $d_i$. If $d_i=0$, the selected slopes at both endpoints of that interval are zero. If $d_i\ne0$, then $m_i/d_i$ and $m_{i+1}/d_i$ both belong to $[0,3]$.

items.title: PCHIP slopes are second-order accurate on uniform nonstationary grids

references.title: F. N. Fritsch and J. Butland, A Method for Constructing Local Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolants, SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 5 (1984), pp. 300–304

items.statement:
Let $a<b$, let $f$ be $C^3$ on an open interval containing $[a,b]$, and suppose $|f'(x)|\ge c>0$ for every $x\in[a,b]$. For an integer $N\ge2$, put $h=(b-a)/N>0$ and $x_j=a+jh$ for $j=0,\ldots,N$. Let $m_j$ be the slopes selected by [[alg-pchip-slope-selection]] from the values $f(x_j)$. There are constants $C,h_0>0$, depending on $f$, $c$, and $[a,b]$, such that for every such grid with $h<h_0$,
$$\max_{0\le j\le N}|m_j-f'(x_j)|\le Ch^2.$$

items.title: PCHIP is C1, monotone on each data segment, and has no interval overshoot

references.title: F. N. Fritsch and J. Butland, A Method for Constructing Local Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolants, SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 5 (1984), pp. 300–304

items.statement: For every input to [[alg-pchip-slope-selection]], the resulting interpolant is $C^1$ and interpolates all input values. On each cell with nonzero secant $d_i$, the interpolant is monotone from $y_i$ to $y_{i+1}$ and stays between those endpoint values; on a cell with $d_i=0$ it is constant. In particular, if the input values are nondecreasing (respectively nonincreasing), the complete interpolant is nondecreasing (respectively nonincreasing). No $C^2$ matching is asserted.

items.title: PCHIP has third-order value accuracy on uniform nonstationary grids

references.title: F. N. Fritsch and J. Butland, A Method for Constructing Local Monotone Piecewise Cubic Interpolants, SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 5 (1984), pp. 300–304
Carl R. de Boor, A Practical Guide to Splines, revised edition, Chapter IV, pp. 39–40

items.statement:
Let $a<b$, let $f$ be $C^3$ on an open interval containing $[a,b]$, and suppose $|f'(x)|\ge c>0$ on $[a,b]$. For each integer $N\ge2$, put $h=(b-a)/N>0$ and $x_j=a+jh$, $j=0,\ldots,N$, and let $P_h$ be the PCHIP interpolant to the values $f(x_j)$. There are constants $C,h_0>0$, depending only on $f$, $c$, and $[a,b]$, such that for every such grid with $h<h_0$,
$$\max_{x\in[a,b]}|P_h(x)-f(x)|\le Ch^3.$$
The assertion is limited to uniform grids and intervals on which the derivative stays bounded away from zero; it makes no third-order claim at an extremum.

title: Shape preserving piecewise polynomial interpolation — Examples

items.title: Positive endpoint samples do not ensure a positive interpolant
items.statement: The quadratic $p(t)=t^2-t+1/10$ is positive at both sampled endpoints $t=0,1$ but negative at $t=1/2$. Its degree-two Bernstein controls are $1/10,-2/5,1/10$; the negative middle control explains why the all-controls-nonnegative hypothesis in [[thm-bernstein-convex-hull-and-positivity]] does not apply.

items.title: A natural cubic spline undershoots a nonnegative table
items.statement:
Consider the nonnegative table $(x_i,y_i)=((0,1),(1,0),(2,0),(3,1))$. On the three unit cells, with $t=x-i$ on cell $[i,i+1]$, define
$$S_0(t)=1-\frac65t+\frac15t^3,\qquad S_1(t)=-\frac35t(1-t),\qquad S_2(t)=\frac35t+\frac35t^2-\frac15t^3.$$
These pieces form a natural cubic spline interpolating the table, but $S_1(t)<0$ for $0<t<1$. PCHIP on the same data has a flat middle segment at zero and remains between the nonnegative cell endpoints.

items.title: PCHIP preserves a flat part of monotone data
items.statement: For nodes $0,1,2,3$ and values $0,1,1,2$, the PCHIP data are monotone with one flat interval. The algorithm selects slopes $(3/2,0,0,3/2)$, and the interpolant is constant on $[1,2]$ while remaining monotone on the adjoining cells.

items.title: PCHIP loses third-order value accuracy next to a smooth extremum
items.statement: Fix $f(x)=x^2$ on $[-1,1]$. For each integer $n\ge2$, use the uniform grid $x_j=-1+jh$, $j=0,\ldots,2n$, with $h=1/n$. The function is smooth and has a strict extremum at zero. On the cell $[-h,0]$, PCHIP's local maximum error is at least $2h^2/27$, so no uniform $Ch^3$ value-error bound on this fixed interval can hold across the extremum.
